title: Advertising rules for tuition and private education providers
asked: Dr Hamid Razak asked what progress the Ministry of Education has made on sector-specific advertising guidelines for tuition and private education services, whether a code of conduct has been finalised, what its key provisions are, and how compliance will be monitored and enforced to protect parents and students from fear-based marketing.
response: MOE is reviewing what measures are needed to discourage undesirable advertising practices by tuition and private education providers. Existing advertisements, including for tuition, are already covered by the Singapore Code of Advertising Practice, which requires ads to be legal, decent, honest and truthful and says they should not capitalise on anxieties to induce demand. MOE has made shifts to reduce the over-emphasis on academic results and will engage parents, students and educators in the coming months on reducing the "arms race" in education.
